claim: A prior disclosure under 19 CFR 162.74 is made when a person discloses the circumstances of a violation before, or without knowledge of, a formal investigation and tenders any actual loss of duties.
publisher: Office of the Federal Register / National Archives (eCFR)
evidence: § 162.74(a): a person "discloses the circumstances of a violation" before, or without knowledge of, a formal investigation, and tenders actual loss.

claim: An oral prior disclosure must be confirmed in writing within 10 days of the date of the oral disclosure.
publisher: Office of the Federal Register / National Archives (eCFR)
evidence: "within 10 days of the date of the oral disclosure."

claim: A prior disclosure must identify the merchandise and the entries or drawback claims involved and specify the material false statements, omissions or acts, including how and when they occurred.
publisher: Office of the Federal Register / National Archives (eCFR)
evidence: "Specifies the material false statements, omissions or acts including an explanation as to how and when they occurred."

claim: Information unknown at the time of disclosure may be provided within 30 days of the initial disclosure, and extensions of the 30-day period may be requested from the Fines, Penalties, and Forfeitures Officer.
publisher: Office of the Federal Register / National Archives (eCFR)
evidence: "provide any information or data unknown at the time of disclosure within 30 days" ... "Extensions of the 30-day period may be requested"

claim: The disclosing party may tender the loss of duties at the time of disclosure or within 30 days after CBP notifies the person in writing of its calculation.
publisher: Office of the Federal Register / National Archives (eCFR)
evidence: "within 30 days after CBP notifies the person in writing."

claim: A prior disclosure sent by registered or certified mail, return receipt requested, is deemed made at the time of mailing; disclosures sent by other methods, including in-person delivery, are deemed made when received by Customs.
publisher: Office of the Federal Register / National Archives (eCFR)
evidence: § 162.74(d): "sent by registered or certified mail" ... "deemed to have been made at the time of mailing"; other methods: "at the time of receipt by Customs"
verifier_note: Corrected by verifier-V8: the mailing rule in § 162.74(d)(1) applies only to registered or certified mail with return receipt; claim and sentence narrowed, then verified.

claim: A written prior disclosure should be addressed to the Commissioner of Customs and presented to a Customs officer at the port of entry of the disclosed violation.
publisher: Office of the Federal Register / National Archives (eCFR)
evidence: "should be addressed to the Commissioner of Customs" ... "presented to a Customs officer at the Customs port of entry of the disclosed violation."

claim: A formal investigation is considered commenced on the date recorded in writing by Customs when facts caused it to believe a possible violation existed.
publisher: Office of the Federal Register / National Archives (eCFR)
evidence: "the date recorded in writing by the Customs Service"

claim: The disclosing party has the burden to prove lack of knowledge of a formal investigation, and knowledge is presumed if the merchandise was seized or Customs issued a prepenalty or penalty notice.
publisher: Office of the Federal Register / National Archives (eCFR)
evidence: "has the burden to prove that lack of knowledge." ... "was seized." ... "Customs issues a prepenalty or penalty notice"

claim: With a valid prior disclosure, a fraud penalty is one times the loss of duties, taxes and fees (or 10 percent of dutiable value if no loss), and a negligence or gross negligence penalty is limited to interest.
publisher: Office of the Federal Register / National Archives (eCFR)
evidence: "One times the loss of duties, taxes and fees" ... 10 percent of dutiable value ... gross negligence and negligence: limited to interest
verifier_note: Penalty levels are in § 162.73(b), on the same subpart G page.

claim: Liquidation is the final computation or ascertainment of duties on entries for consumption or drawback entries.
publisher: Office of the Federal Register / National Archives (eCFR)
evidence: "the final computation or ascertainment of duties on entries for consumption or drawback entries."

claim: Notice of liquidation of formal entries is provided on CBP's public website, and that posting is deemed the legal evidence of liquidation.
publisher: Office of the Federal Register / National Archives (eCFR)
evidence: "Notice of liquidation of formal entries will be provided on CBP's public Web site" ... "deemed the legal evidence of liquidation"

claim: An entry not liquidated within one year from the date of entry is deemed liquidated at the rate, value, quantity and amount of duties asserted by the importer of record.
publisher: Office of the Federal Register / National Archives (eCFR)
evidence: "at the rate of duty, value, quantity, and amount of duties asserted by the importer of record" ... "the date of entry of the merchandise"

claim: The one-year liquidation period may be extended by up to 1 year at a time, total extensions may not exceed 3 years, and an entry not liquidated within four years is deemed liquidated unless liquidation is suspended.
publisher: Office of the Federal Register / National Archives (eCFR)
evidence: "an additional period not to exceed 1 year" ... "may not exceed 3 years" ... four years: deemed liquidated unless suspended

claim: Protestable decisions include appraised value; classification and rate and amount of duties; liquidation or reliquidation; and the refusal to pay a claim for drawback.
publisher: Office of the Federal Register / National Archives (eCFR)
evidence: "The appraised value of merchandise;" "The classification and rate and amount of duties chargeable;" ... "The refusal to pay a claim for drawback;"

claim: Those who may file a protest include the importer or consignee shown on the entry papers or their sureties, any person filing a drawback claim, and authorized agents.
publisher: Office of the Federal Register / National Archives (eCFR)
evidence: "The importer or consignee shown on the entry papers, or their sureties;" ... "Any person filing a claim for drawback;"

claim: For entries made on or after December 18, 2004, a protest must be filed within 180 days of the decision, counted from the date of notice of liquidation or reliquidation (or of liquidation itself) or the date of the decision.
publisher: Office of the Federal Register / National Archives (eCFR)
evidence: "within 180 days of a decision relating to an entry made on or after December 18, 2004"

claim: A protest must state the protestant's name and address, importer number, entry number and date, liquidation date, a specific description of the merchandise, and the grounds for each objection.
publisher: Office of the Federal Register / National Archives (eCFR)
evidence: § 174.13: name and address, importer number, entry number and date, liquidation date, description of merchandise, specific grounds for each objection.

claim: CBP generally must act on a protest within 2 years from the date it was filed.
publisher: Office of the Federal Register / National Archives (eCFR)
evidence: "within 2 years from the date the protest was filed"

claim: If CBP does not act within 30 days after a request for accelerated disposition is mailed, the protest is deemed denied at the close of the 30th day.
publisher: Office of the Federal Register / National Archives (eCFR)
evidence: § 174.22: "deemed to have been denied at the close of the 30th day following such date of mailing"
verifier_note: Corrected by verifier-V8: wording aligned with § 174.22(d) ('close of the 30th day'); verified.

claim: Further review may be sought where the decision conflicts with a prior ruling on similar merchandise, involves unresolved questions of law or fact, or presents new facts or arguments.
publisher: Office of the Federal Register / National Archives (eCFR)
evidence: § 174.24: conflicts with a prior ruling or decision on similar merchandise, unresolved questions of law or fact, or new facts or arguments.
verifier_note: Verified against § 174.24(a)-(c). Page phrase 'above the Center director level' was uncited and removed.

claim: After a protest is denied, the protestant may file a civil action in the United States Court of International Trade within 180 days after the denial.
publisher: Office of the Federal Register / National Archives (eCFR)
evidence: "within 180 days after" ... "filing a civil action in the United States Court of International Trade"

claim: Paper protests are filed on CBP Form 19, and electronic filing through CBP-authorized systems is accepted.
publisher: Office of the Federal Register / National Archives (eCFR)
evidence: § 174.12: paper protests on CBP Form 19 in four copies; electronic filing through CBP's authorized systems also accepted.
